sections.html:
Muskogee County sits in northeast Oklahoma, and the city of Muskogee is both seat and largest town. It covers 840 square miles and belongs to the Tulsa-Muskogee-Bartlesville area. The 2020 Census counted 66,339 residents in 25,525 households and 29,278 housing units, of which 12.8 percent were vacant. Owners live in 64.8 percent of occupied homes and renters in 35.2 percent, so a good share of sales involve landlords, heirs and empty houses.

Haskell and Muskogee are the cities. Towns include Boynton, Braggs, Council Hill, Fort Gibson, Oktaha, Porum, Summit, Taft, Wainwright, Warner and Webbers Falls. Interstate 40, US 62, 64 and 69, State Highways 2, 10, 16 and 72 and the Muskogee Turnpike all cross the county.

School districts are Braggs, Checotah, Fort Gibson, Gore, Haskell, Hilldale, Midway, Muskogee, Oktaha, Porum, Warner and Webbers Falls, plus Wainwright for elementary grades. Property in Fort Gibson, Muskogee and Hilldale schools can carry different levies, so check the district printed on your own statement.

Two offices handle your tax account. The treasurer answers questions about payoffs and payments, while the assessor answers questions about value and exemptions.

OfficeContactHours
Treasurer400 West Broadway, Room 220, Muskogee, OK 74401, 918-682-0811Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM
Assessor918-682-8781, assessor@muskogeeassessor.com, muskogeeassessor.comCall for hours

The assessor's website shows the current year's levies and how a payment splits among the taxing bodies. The treasurer's tax roll search lets you look up unpaid taxes by owner name, street address, parcel number or school district. Start with the treasurer's tax roll search or the assessor's tax information page.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
Think of the bill as three steps. First the assessor puts a value on the parcel. Then the Excise Board certifies the millage. Last, the treasurer sends a single statement and distributes the receipts to the county, the city or town, and the schools. One mill equals $1 for every $1,000 of taxable value, with assessment ratios between 10 and 15 percent.

Where the owner lives in the house, $1,000 is removed from taxable value and assessed value may climb only 3 percent a year until the home changes hands. A sale wipes out that cap, which is why a buyer can open a bill larger than the one you paid.

Muskogee County also has more than one school district inside its lines, and the levy rides on whichever one your address falls in. Find the district on the statement itself.

  • Values come from the assessor's records and inspections.
  • Levies come from each taxing body.
  • Payment goes to the treasurer in one or two installments.

Statements can be paid starting November 1. The county wants half in hand before January 1, with the rest following before April 1. If the first half does not arrive in time, delinquency covers the whole bill from January 1 on.

  • Interest builds at 1.5 percent a month and tops out at 100 percent of the unpaid tax.
  • A total of $25 or less is due in one payment before January 1.
  • Mortgage servicers send one payment a year, before January 1.
  • On mailed payments the treasurer stamps the date received, and interest stops once the envelope arrives.

Debit cards online cost 1.95 percent and credit cards 2.75 percent, charged by the processor and not by the treasurer. A check, or a visit to the window, avoids that fee.

Your protest goes to the assessor in writing. After a notice of higher value, count 30 calendar days from the date it was mailed. With no change in value, the cutoff is the first Monday in April.

The assessor has to hold an informal hearing, offer at least two other dates if you cannot make the first, and put a decision in writing within 7 calendar days. If you still disagree, you have 15 calendar days to appeal to the county board of equalization. Include the valuation information the form requires, or the assessor's figure is presumed correct.

Photos of damage, repair quotes and recent sales of similar houses strengthen a protest.

Whatever tax is owed gets paid from your proceeds when the sale closes, based on a figure from the treasurer. Cities can also certify liens for weeds, cleanup, paving and nuisance abatement to the county treasurer, so ask for those amounts too.

  1. Search the tax roll for every year, not only the current one.
  2. Ask the treasurer for a payoff in writing.
  3. Ask whether any city weed or cleanup charges were certified to the county.
  4. Confirm the school district on the bill before you quote taxes to a buyer.

Do this before you set a price. The net figure on your closing statement depends on it.

sections.h2: Steps for selling a tenant-occupied or inherited house
sections.html:
Muskogee County has a lot of rentals and empty houses, so the sale often starts with a situation rather than a plan. A landlord may want out of a house with a tenant on a lease. An heir may live in another state and never have seen the house in years. Both can work through the same short list.

  1. Pull the parcel on the tax roll to see the tax history.
  2. Find out who is on the deed, or whether probate has to finish first.
  3. Gather the lease, keys, repair history and any city notices.
  4. Decide whether to list with an agent or take an as-is cash offer.
  5. Have the settlement agent clear taxes and liens from the proceeds.

Muskogee, Fort Gibson and Haskell each have their own city offices, and a city lien is separate from county tax. Ask the right city whether anything is open on the address.

Typical sellers are landlords with tenants in place, heirs to older houses in Muskogee and Fort Gibson, and owners with deferred repairs. With 35.2 percent of occupied homes rented and 12.8 percent of all units vacant, many houses here are not owner-occupied.

An as-is cash sale skips listing prep and lender-required repairs. A buyer paying cash can close without waiting for a retail inspection, which helps when tenants are still in the house or when an estate wants to wrap up. Before you accept any offer, get a written payoff for taxes and for any city liens so you know what you will keep.

If tenants occupy the house, tell the buyer up front and bring a copy of the lease. If the house is vacant, expect questions about utilities, break-ins and how long it has sat.

faqs.q: Where is the Muskogee County treasurer?
faqs.a: The treasurer is at 400 West Broadway, Room 220 in Muskogee, phone 918-682-0811, open Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

faqs.q: When are Muskogee County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are payable November 1. Half must be paid before January 1 and the rest before April 1.

faqs.q: Does Muskogee County charge fees to pay online?
faqs.a: Yes. The processor charges 1.95 percent on debit cards and 2.75 percent on credit cards, and the treasurer's office does not keep these fees.

faqs.q: How do I protest my property value?
faqs.a: File a written protest with the assessor within 30 calendar days of an increase notice, or by the first Monday in April if the value did not change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Muskogee County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent tax and interest are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
